item.title: Trade wars destroy the planet
item.description: Given that China is the world’s largest emitter and has a high carbon intensity, some assume that its trade war with the United States, which has shifted production to third countries, would have environmental benefits. In fact, the conflict has increased carbon dioxide emissions in developing and advanced economies alike.

item.title: Malaysia’s chip boom risks soaring Scope 2 emissions, experts warn
item.description: At the Semiconductor Sustainability Summit 2025, industry leaders said Malaysia’s push to double its global chip share could deepen electricity and water pressures unless fabs overhaul how they source, use and conserve energy.

item.title: Asean races ahead of the US and Europe in EV adoption: study
item.description: Southeast Asian is emerging as a global hotspot for electric vehicle adoption, with several countries in the region overtaking the United States and parts of Europe in the share of EVs sold, according to new analysis.

item.title: Global shipping’s top lenders are getting increasingly aligned to IMO’s net zero target: study
item.description: Thirty-six international banks, including Japanese and Singapore funders, are closer to following the trajectory of the International Maritime Organization’s emissions goal, found a report by the Poseidon Principles.

item.title: Singapore dominates Southeast Asia’s green startup landscape, report finds
item.description: New mapping of climate firms shows region rich in solutions but constrained by grids, finance and coordination.

item.title: India’s food waste is turning into an environmental time bomb
item.description: India’s colossal food waste problem is both a symptom and a significant accelerator of the climate crisis.

item.title: Three reasons why China wants global green leadership after COP30
item.description: China wants to lead the climate agenda on its own terms – exporting clean tech and influence, while sidestepping tougher cuts and accountability.

item.title: A year of Gen Z protests: Can they bring real change in 2026?
item.description: Gen Z protesters are shaking governments worldwide but experts wonder if rage can lead to lasting reform.

item.title: Arthur Joseph Kurup appointed as Malaysia’s new environment minister
item.description: He takes the helm of the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability ministry following a Cabinet reshuffle, succeeding acting minister Johari Abdul Ghani and former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad.

item.title: South Korea to include plastic toys in recycling responsibility scheme from 2026
item.description: Move brings 18 toy categories under extended producer responsibility rules as Seoul steps up efforts to cut plastic wastes.
